title: Sound Teaching and Mercy for Sinners
summary_text: Paul tells Timothy to remain in Ephesus and stop false teaching, myths, and arguments about genealogies, since sound instruction aims at love and sincere faith. The law rightly addresses lawless conduct, in line with the gospel entrusted to Paul. Once violent and a persecutor, Paul received mercy and overflowing grace from Christ Jesus, who came to save sinners. Calling himself the worst of them, he presents Christ's patience toward him as an example for future believers receiving eternal life. He charges Timothy to hold faith and a clear conscience, unlike Hymenaeus and Alexander, whom he handed to Satan to learn not to blaspheme.
key_points: Timothy must stop speculative teaching and promote love from a pure heart, clear conscience, and sincere faith.
The law addresses lawless conduct, including murder, sexual immorality, same-sex acts, slave trading, and lying.
Christ showed Paul mercy and grace despite his violent past, displaying patience toward sinners who would receive eternal life.
Paul urges Timothy to guard faith and conscience, unlike two men handed to Satan to learn not to blaspheme.

title: Prayer for All and Conduct in Worship
summary_text: Paul urges prayer for everyone, including rulers, so believers can live peaceful lives in godliness. God wants everyone saved, and Christ Jesus is the one mediator between God and humanity, who gave Himself as a ransom for all. Paul wants men to pray with holy hands and without anger, and women to show modesty and good deeds rather than costly display. He directs women to learn quietly and submissively, forbidding them to teach or exercise authority over men, and points to Adam's creation before Eve and her transgression after deception. He says women will be saved through childbearing if they continue in faith, love, holiness, and self-control.
key_points: Prayer for everyone, including rulers, seeks peaceful lives in godliness and pleases God, who wants all people saved.
Christ Jesus is the one mediator and gave Himself as a ransom for all; Paul was appointed an apostle.
Paul calls men to prayer without anger and women to modest dress and deeds fitting their worship of God.

title: Qualifications for Leaders in God's Household
summary_text: An overseer must have a good reputation, self-control, gentleness, skill in teaching, and a well-managed household, since he will care for God's church. He must not be newly converted or greedy, and must avoid pride and the devil's traps. Deacons must likewise be tested, honest, and responsible at home, holding the faith with a clear conscience; the women must be dignified and faithful. Paul gives these instructions so Timothy knows proper conduct in God's household, which upholds the truth. He ends with the confession of godliness: Christ appeared in flesh, was vindicated by the Spirit, seen by angels, proclaimed and believed in, and taken into glory.
key_points: An overseer needs proven character, teaching ability, wise household management, and a good name among outsiders.
Deacons must be tested, hold the faith with a clear conscience, and manage their families well.

title: Timothy Must Teach and Model the Faith
summary_text: The Spirit warns that some will abandon the faith for teachings of demons, including bans on marriage and certain foods. God made food to be received thankfully, and it is sanctified by His word and prayer. Timothy must reject empty myths and train in godliness, which has value both now and in the life to come. Though young, he must model faith and pure conduct, read Scripture publicly, teach, and develop his gift. By watching his life and teaching and persevering, he will save himself and his hearers.
key_points: Deceitful spirits will lead some away from the faith into false rules against marriage and foods God created.
Food received with thanks is sanctified through God's word and prayer.
As Christ's servant, Timothy must train in godliness and place his hope in the living God, the Savior.

title: Care for Widows and Treat Elders Fairly
summary_text: Paul tells Timothy to treat believers as family, with respect and purity. Families must care for their widows so the church can help those truly alone and in need. Widows enrolled for support must meet the standards Paul gives; younger widows are urged to marry rather than drift from Christ into idle lives. Elders who lead well deserve honor and pay, while charges need witnesses and ongoing sin needs open rebuke without bias. Timothy must keep pure, avoid haste in laying on hands, and remember that sins and good deeds will come to light.
key_points: Timothy must approach older and younger believers as family members and treat women with purity.
Failure to provide for one's household denies the faith, while family care leaves the church free to help needy widows.
Older widows with faithful lives may be enrolled; younger widows are advised to marry and manage their households.
Effective elders deserve honor and wages; accusations need witnesses, and persistent sin requires public correction without bias.

title: Pursue Godliness Rather Than the Love of Money
summary_text: Paul instructs slaves to honor their masters so God's name and the teaching are not discredited. False teachers stir up quarrels and treat godliness as a way to profit, but contentment is true gain, while love of money draws people from the faith. Timothy must pursue righteousness, hold to eternal life, and keep the commandment until Jesus Christ appears at the time God sets. Paul praises God as the only immortal ruler and tells the rich to hope in Him and share generously. Timothy must guard what was entrusted to him and reject empty talk and false knowledge.
key_points: Slaves must honor their masters, including believing masters, so God's name and teaching are not discredited.
False teaching breeds conflict, while love of money brings temptation, ruin, and departure from the faith.

God, the only immortal ruler, will bring Christ's appearing at His own time.
